text: Burst firing in the lateral habenula (LHb) is enhanced under stress and depression, and ketamine blocks burst firing in LHb to exert a rapid antidepressant effect. Thus, burst firing in LHb may serve as a cellular mechanism of depression and a promising therapeutic target for developing novel antidepressants. However, the mechanisms underlying burst firing in LHb are not fully understood. The present study aims to investigate the contribution of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) to burst firing in LHb.
source_label: NMDA receptors are not necessary for burst firing of lateral habenula neurons in mice
